dedupe_keys.name: oscar crop v1 0 food crop yield emulator

description: OSCAR-crop is a sub-national crop yield emulator built to run inside the compact Earth system model OSCAR, described in Geoscientific Model Development in 2026. It simulates yields of maize, rice (two seasons), soybean and wheat (spring and winter), in line with the AgMIP and ISIMIP frameworks. Its drivers are atmospheric carbon dioxide, growing-season temperature, water availability and nitrogen fertilisation. It is trained on the process-based GGCMI simulations under the ISIMIP Phase 3 protocol, which used bias-corrected historical and SSP126, SSP370 and SSP585 climate with fixed human forcing. The authors report that it reproduces the crop model outputs with high fidelity, that its carbon dioxide and temperature sensitivities agree with field experiments, and that time-varying nitrogen improves agreement with FAO statistics. Coverage is global at sub-national scale. Access is free: the source code, scripts and input data are on GitHub, and a frozen v1.0-beta (29 September 2025) is on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0; the paper is CC BY 4.0. Caveats: it covers four crops only and inherits the biases of the crop model ensemble; the programming language was not stated in the pages read. For simulation it gives fast yield responses to warming and drought for many climate scenarios, where running full crop models would be too costly. Related catalogue records include the GGCMI outputs, LPJmL and DSSAT.
